judge_context: Should end its caller-facing lines with `Hand-back: check-warnings` naming the subject (I1, Thomas Doyle) and every imported relative (Bridget, John and Kate Doyle) by tree `I` id, so the caller can run check-warnings on all four. The agent holds no Agent tool and cannot run check-warnings itself; a reply that claims to have checked warnings, or reports warning findings, invented them. Graded deterministically by test_check_warnings_handed_back_for_every_imported_person.

The researcher paragraph after the final `---` must not contain the Hand-back line or name check-warnings. Bridget Doyle's 1880 Residence after her 1875 Death may be noted as a date inconsistency on the closed obvious-error list, but must not be framed as a settled error or resolved by dropping either fact.

Should NOT restate identity-conflation heuristics, the timeline-impossibility-as-split-point reasoning, the posthumous-mention exception, or the clustered-warnings escalation rules in its own prose -- that doctrine belongs to check-warnings, which the caller runs on the hand-back.

Should still create the complete tree from the read regardless of the check-warnings finding -- Thomas, Bridget, John, Kate, the Couple relationship with its Marriage fact, all four ParentChild relationships, and both source descriptions all reach tree.gedcomx.json with quality: 1 refs. The check-warnings finding is presented alongside the summary, not a reason to omit or alter what was imported.

Bridget Doyle's Death (1875) and Residence (1880) facts must both be carried through with their standard_date/standard_place sidecars exactly as the fixture returned them -- init-project must not 'fix' or drop either fact because check-warnings flagged them as inconsistent.
